decision_reason: PS-TB-01 is a property-style rejection claim on the Rust-local pure decode_postcard function. Per references/verifier-trigger-matrix.md, the proptest lane is the primary lane for property claims (rust_local + rejection tags). proptest over arbitrary payloads in [0, MAX_PAYLOAD] and arbitrary trailing lengths in [1, 4096] exercises the strict-length branch in a non-vacuous way with shrink, which is exactly the right tool for the bug-closure property. proptest is already declared in the workspace dev-dependencies (Cargo.toml:40) and as a vb_cli dev-dependency (crates/vb_cli/Cargo.toml:32); the command is runnable after proof-writer wires verification/proptest/properties.rs into a test target.

PS-TB-02 is a unit-test-shaped claim that locks down the variant shape and Display arm. Per references/verifier-trigger-matrix.md, cargo-test is the right tool for variant-shape unit tests: std::mem::discriminant assertion, format!() non-empty check, exact PostcardError::TrailingBytes equality, and the json-propagation regression. cargo-test runs the vb_cli lib tests, including the existing tests.rs module (crates/vb_cli/src/cli_postcard/tests.rs:1-197) and the new tests added by the proof-writer. The acceptance conditions in contract.md (lines 112-118) explicitly require unit tests decode_rejects_trailing_bytes_after_valid_frame and decode_accepts_exact_length_frame to pass, which cargo-test discharges.

PS-TB-08 is a cross-crate parity claim that the fix in vb_cli and the existing strict-length check in vb_ipc::frame::decode_frame_payload agree on the strict-length invariant. cargo-clippy on vb_cli is the primary gate for this claim because it ensures the new code does not introduce any workspace lint violation, matches the cross-crate shape (single-compare pattern), and triggers no clippy::comparison_chain / clippy::manual_strip on the != length check. contract.md acceptance condition 9 (line 119) explicitly names cargo clippy -p vb_cli --all-targets -- -D warnings as a required gate.

PS-TB-03 carries the regression claim that the fix preserves POST-007 (magic + header length validation) and INV-005 (bounded allocation). The moon run :source-lint gate is the canonical CI gate per AGENTS.md and contract.md acceptance condition 10. It composes panic-surface, ignored-fallible-results, unsafe-audit, fmt, and clippy --all-features into a single zero-tolerance pass. The new TrailingBytes variant, the new Display arm, and the != length check must all pass this gate; otherwise the fix is rejected.

Vacuum Verus specs are rejected per AGENTS.md GOD RULE 2. The cli_postcard module has no production-bound Verus spec in verification/verus/ today (verified by rg -n TrailingBytes verification/verus/ which returns zero matches). Adding a standalone spec for one integer compare would be laundering; the property is purely length-equality and is fully discharged by PO-TB-PROP-01 (proptest over [0, MAX_PAYLOAD] x [1, 4096]) plus PO-TB-UNIT-01 (cargo-test on the exact-length / trailing-bytes / variant-shape unit cases). Per references/risk-taxonomy.md the rust_local tag would normally trigger verus, but the absence of a pre-existing production-bound spec plus the triviality of the property (single integer compare) means verus adds no unique evidence.

decision_reason: The fix is a single integer compare: data.len() != payload_end. Flux refinement types apply when the property is a quantifier-free arithmetic predicate expressed as a refinement on a numeric type; the strict-length invariant here is already a single .len() comparison with no refinement surface. Per references/verifier-trigger-matrix.md the Flux counterindication is 'the relationship is dynamic and beyond Flux's decidable fragment' or 'no refinement expresses the property'. The strict-length compare trivially discharges by a single usize .len() call; there is no #[refined_by] candidate. Per references/tooling-availability-gate.md cargo-flux is also not pinned in the workspace.
